q: 1. Darcy's law is applicable to seepage if a soil is
explain: Darcy's law assumptions include a homogeneous, isotropic, saturated, incompressible medium with laminar flow — all conditions must hold.

q: 2. The maximum pressure which a soil can carry without shear failure, is called
explain: Safe bearing capacity is the maximum pressure the soil can safely carry without shear failure, incorporating a factor of safety.

q: 3. The time required for the completion of consolidation for a thin soil sample when compared with that of a thick soil sample will be .............
explain: Per the reference key this is left indeterminate; generally, thinner samples with shorter drainage paths consolidate faster than thicker ones.

q: 4. The change in the thickness of a soil sample may be due to .............
options: expulsion of pore water or pore air from the voids
compression of the soil solid particles
compression of water (or) air in the voids of soil
explain: Volume change in soil during consolidation is primarily due to expulsion of pore water/air from the voids, not compression of the solids themselves.

q: 5. The process of compaction of a soil involves .............
options: expulsion of both pore water and air voids
explain: Compaction (a mechanical process) primarily expels air from the voids; pore water removal instead characterizes consolidation.

q: 6. The property of the soil which allows to flow water through the soil is known as
explain: Permeability is the soil property governing the ease with which water can flow through its interconnected voids.

q: 7. The active earth pressure of a soil can be defined as lateral pressure exerted by the soil when
options: the retaining wall tends to move away from the back fill
wall moves relative to the back fill
explain: Active earth pressure develops when the wall yields/moves away from the backfill, allowing the soil to expand and mobilize its shear strength to a minimum pressure state.

q: 8. The lateral earth pressure of the soil moves towards the retaining wall indicates
explain: When the soil mass itself tends to move toward (push against) the wall while the wall yields away, this describes the active earth pressure condition.

q: 9. The base width of retaining wall is B. What is the maximum, permissible eccentricity if the wall should not fail in tension?
explain: To avoid tension at the base (keeping the resultant within the middle third), the eccentricity must not exceed B/6, per the middle-third rule for rectangular sections.

q: 10. Earth pressure acting at a height of ........ in case of inclined surcharge
options: h/2 from the base of the wall
h/3 from the base of the wall
h/4 from the base of the wall
h/5 from the base of the wall
explain: For a wall with inclined surcharge, the resultant earth pressure (trapezoidal-type distribution due to surcharge) acts at approximately h/4 above the base, as per standard design charts.

q: 11. The assumption of Rankine's theory of earth pressure is
options: the soil is semi finite, homogeneous, dry and cohesionless
ground surface is a plane which may be inclined or horizontal
back of the wall is vertical and smooth
explain: Rankine's theory assumes a semi-infinite, homogeneous, cohesionless, dry soil mass, a planar ground surface, and a vertical, smooth wall back — all these assumptions together define the theory.

q: 12. Bearing capacity of soil is determined by
options: both a. and b. of above
explain: Both the plate load test and standard (cone) penetration test are recognized field methods for estimating bearing capacity of soil.

q: 13. The soil having minimum/least bearing capacity is
explain: Moist (saturated) clay has very low shear strength and high compressibility, giving it the least bearing capacity among the listed soil types.

q: 14. Who is known as the Father of 'Soil Mechanics'?
explain: Karl Terzaghi is universally credited as the 'Father of Soil Mechanics' for founding the discipline with his effective stress principle and consolidation theory.

q: 15. When a static load is applied, the consolidation is fast the case of .............
explain: Sands have high permeability, allowing pore water to drain and consolidation to occur almost instantaneously compared to fine-grained soils.

q: 16. The minimum number of observation wells required to determine the permeability of stratum in the field by pumping test is .............
explain: At least two observation wells at different radial distances are needed to establish the drawdown curve and calculate permeability.

q: 17. Darcy's law is applicable if a soil is .............
explain: Darcy's law assumptions require the soil to be homogeneous, incompressible, and isotropic for validity of the linear flow relation.

q: 18. According to Darcy's law, the flow velocity can be obtained by .............
explain: Darcy's law states discharge velocity v = Ki (permeability times hydraulic gradient).

q: 19. A combined footing is generally used when
options: Number of columns is more than two and they are spaced far apart
Number of columns is two and they are spaced far close to each other
Number of columns is two and they are spaced far apart
explain: A combined footing is provided when two columns are close enough that their individual isolated footings would overlap, so a single combined footing supports both.

q: 20. The depth upto which the stress increment due to the applied loads can produce significant settlement is called as .............
explain: Significant depth is the term for the zone below a foundation where applied stress increments meaningfully contribute to settlement.

q: 21. The minimum depth of exploration in case of gravity dam is .............
explain: For gravity dams, exploration typically extends to a depth roughly equal to the height of the dam to characterize the stressed foundation zone.

q: 22. Rankin's theory of earth pressure assumes that, back of the wall is
explain: Rankine's theory assumes the back face of the retaining wall is vertical and perfectly smooth (frictionless), simplifying the stress analysis to principal stress conditions.

q: 23. The coefficient of active earth pressure for loose sand having an angle of internal friction of 30° is
24. A comparatively sudden reduction in volume of a soil mass under an applied load (due principally to expulsion and compression of gas in the soil voids preceding primary consolidation) is called
explain: This rapid initial volume reduction, occurring due to compression/expulsion of air before true primary consolidation begins, is termed initial consolidation.

q: 25. Rise in water table upto the ground surface results in .............
options: reduction of pore water pressure but no change in total stress
increase of pore water pressure and increase in total stress
increase of pore water pressure and increase in total stress
increase of pore water pressure and decrease in total stress
explain: As water table rises, both total stress (due to submerged unit weight change) and pore pressure increase together.

q: 26. The number of heads that are used for defining the water head at a point in a soil mass are .............
explain: Total head at a point is composed of three components: elevation head, pressure head, and velocity head.

q: 27. The pore water pressure in the capillary zone is .............
explain: Water held in the capillary fringe above the water table is under suction (tension), giving it negative pore water pressure.

q: 28. In most of the practical flow problems in soil mechanics, the flow is .............
explain: Given the very low seepage velocities in soils, flow is almost always laminar, satisfying the basis for Darcy's law.

options: a curve connecting points of equal vertical pressure
a point at which the net pressure is zero
a curve connecting points of equal pore water pressure
explain: An isobar (pressure bulb contour) is a curve connecting points of equal vertical stress increment below a loaded area.

q: 30. Rise of water table above the ground surface causes .............
options: equal increase in pore water pressure and total stress
equal increase in pore water pressure and effective stress
equal increase in total stress and effective stress
explain: Per the reference key, flooding above ground surface produces an equal rise in total stress and effective stress at a given point.

q: 31. Physical properties of a permeant which influences the permeability are .............
explain: Permeability depends on the permeant fluid's unit weight and viscosity together, as seen in k = C.d^2.gamma/mu.

q: 32. The time required for full dissipation of pore water pressure will depend on .............
options: co-efficient of permeability of soil only
both thickness and co-efficient of permeability only
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'none of the above'; per consolidation theory (Tv = Cv.t/d^2), dissipation time depends on both layer thickness and permeability (via Cv).

q: 33. The seepage force in a soil is .............
explain: Seepage force acts in the direction of flow, which is perpendicular to the equipotential lines.

q: 34. A soil which is fully consolidated under the existing over burden pressure is known as .............
explain: A soil fully consolidated under its present overburden (with no excess pore pressure remaining) is defined as normally consolidated.

q: 35. The relationship between the time factor Tv, coefficient of consolidation Cv, the length of drainage path d, and time t is given by .............
explain: Time factor is defined as Tv = Cv.t/d^2, a dimensionless parameter combining consolidation coefficient, time, and drainage path length.

q: 36. The neutral stress on the soil is due to .............
options: Weight of water present in soil pores
external load acting on the soil
explain: Neutral stress (pore water pressure) is caused by the water present in the soil voids, exerting hydrostatic pressure on grains.
